name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,806

entries.clue: Motor home’s grand, a trendy thing (6)

blocks.note: G = grand, as in a thousand pounds

annotation.surface: A glossy camper van is described as a grand, fashionable possession.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Motor home' looks like a camper van, but here it is where a motor car lives. The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A garage is the building where a car is kept, so it is literally a home for a motor.

entries.clue: Section of chart for making e.g. music (3,4)

indicatorNotes.Section of: the answer is a section cut from the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of 'chart', all of 'for' and the start of 'making'

annotation.surface: A composer describes the part of a score used to produce a piece of music.
annotation.walkthrough: The run of letters crosses two word breaks, which is how a hidden answer disguises itself.
annotation.definitionFit: Music is one example of an art form, which the 'e.g.' signals.

entries.clue: Is it manic, misguided, seeing a soul in everything? (9)

indicatorNotes.misguided: the letters are led astray into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether believing everything has a soul is a sign of a deranged mind.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder is the first three words; the question mark lets the surface read as a sceptic's jibe.
annotation.definitionFit: Animism is the belief that objects and natural things have souls, so an animistic view sees a soul in everything.

entries.clue: Cover a lot of jealousy and run off with loved one (8)

indicatorNotes.a lot of: most, but not all, of the word: ENVY loses its last letter

blocks.note: to elope is to run away with a lover to marry

annotation.surface: A jealous lover hides their feelings and runs away with their sweetheart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cover' is a verb in the surface but the noun sense, the paper cover of a letter, is wanted.
annotation.definitionFit: An envelope is a cover for a letter, or anything that encloses something.

entries.clue: Backing for soul number that’s irrational and ridiculous (6)

indicatorNotes.Backing for: the word for 'soul' is turned back to front

blocks.note: the ba is the soul in ancient Egyptian belief
a surd is an irrational number such as the square root of 2

annotation.surface: A backing band for a soul song is dismissed as unreasonable and silly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Soul' and 'number' suggest music, but the soul is Egyptian and the number is mathematical.
annotation.definitionFit: Absurd means ridiculous, wildly unreasonable.

entries.clue: Attractiveness of everything on river in The Dales (6)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the next

blocks.note: the Ure is a Yorkshire river that runs through Wensleydale

annotation.surface: A travel writer praises the total charm of a river running through the Yorkshire Dales.
annotation.walkthrough: The Yorkshire Dales are an upland area of northern England; the River Ure is one of their rivers.
annotation.definitionFit: Allure is the quality of being attractive or enticing.

entries.clue: Special ice cream cake (5)

blocks.note: S = special, as in S for special constable

annotation.surface: A café menu offers a special frozen cake.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one dish, an ice cream cake; split it after 'ice cream'. A scone is a small British baked cake eaten with jam and cream.
annotation.definitionFit: A scone is a small plain cake, often served with tea.

entries.clue: Could this drink be nastier? (7)

indicatorNotes.Could: 'could ... be' asks what the letters might become if rearranged
indicatorNotes.be: completes 'could ... be': the fodder may be made into the answer

annotation.surface: A drinker winces and wonders if any drink could taste worse.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: retsina, a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin, has a taste many find unpleasant.
annotation.definitionFit: Retsina's resinous taste has a reputation for being an acquired one, so it is the drink the question points at.

entries.clue: How we speak arranging pact or in union ... (13)

indicatorNotes.arranging: the letters are put into a new order

annotation.surface: A trade union drafting a pact is urged to agree on how its members talk.
annotation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue on into 9 down, and together they name the song theme of the puzzle.
annotation.definitionFit: Pronunciation is the way words are spoken.

entries.clue: ... disputes -  resistance remaining in reorganised sections (13)

indicatorNotes.in: R and OVER go inside the rearranged letters
indicatorNotes.reorganised: the letters of SECTIONS are put in a new order

blocks.note: SECTIONS rearranged, then split around ROVER

annotation.surface: An office row over resistance to a restructure lingers on in the reorganised departments.
annotation.walkthrough: Read with 8 down: pronunciation controversies are the subject of the song 'Let's Call the Whole Thing Off' (15 across, 22 down).
annotation.definitionFit: Controversies are disputes, especially public ones.

entries.clue: Bringing back opportunity to 28 about English version (9)

indicatorNotes.about: RETRIAL goes around the other letters

blocks.note: 28 across is REHEAR; a retrial is a chance to rehear a case

annotation.surface: A court grants a chance to rehear a case about an English translation.
annotation.walkthrough: The cross-reference sends you to REHEAR; a retrial is the chance to rehear, and E and V are slotted in after its fifth letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: retrieving something means fetching it back, as a dog retrieves a stick.

entries.clue: Run rings round picnic? (5)

blocks.note: to beat someone with ease, making them look slow
split in two: an outdoor party, a 'do' held in the open air

annotation.surface: Someone plans to dash in circles around a picnic spread.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second reading: a picnic is an 'out do', a party held outdoors.
annotation.definitionFit: To run rings round someone is to beat them easily, which is to outdo them.

entries.clue: I complain about pleasant girl (5)

indicatorNotes.about: the phrase is turned about, back to front

annotation.surface: Someone grumbles about a nice young woman.
annotation.walkthrough: I MOAN reads backwards as NAOMI. The name Naomi means 'pleasant' in Hebrew, which is why the definition is 'pleasant girl' rather than just 'girl'.
annotation.definitionFit: Naomi is a girl's name whose Hebrew meaning is 'pleasant'.

entries.clue: Not even caring, I steal with abandon (9)

annotation.definition: Not even caring, I steal with abandon

indicatorNotes.Not even: keep the odd letters of 'caring', dropping the even ones
indicatorNotes.with abandon: the letters are thrown about freely into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, used as it stands

annotation.surface: A thief confesses to stealing recklessly, without a thought for anyone.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well: a thief who steals without caring is a larcenist. 'Not even' reads as 'not at all', but it means the odd letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Larceny is theft, so a larcenist is someone who steals.

entries.clue: Tame bats held by back of neck - you'll need to get a handle on it (8)

annotation.definition: you'll need to get a handle on it

indicatorNotes.bats: bats = crazy, so the letters are scrambled
indicatorNotes.held by: the scrambled letters sit inside NAPE

blocks.note: the nape is the back of the neck

annotation.surface: Someone holds tame bats against the back of their neck and is told to get a grip.
annotation.walkthrough: A handle is slang for a name, so a name tape is the label sewn into clothing that you write a name on. British school uniforms carry them.
annotation.definitionFit: A name tape carries your name, which is your 'handle'.

entries.clue: It makes a sauce accompanied by potato in 8 9 song (6)

blocks.note: a red fruit cooked down for pasta and ketchup
8 9 is PRONUNCIATION CONTROVERSIES; the song pairs this word with potato, each said two ways

annotation.surface: A recipe note: this goes into a sauce, alongside potato in a famous song.
annotation.walkthrough: 8 9 is PRONUNCIATION CONTROVERSIES; the song is Gershwin's 'Let's Call the Whole Thing Off', built on differing pronunciations of words like potato and tomato.
annotation.definitionFit: Tomatoes are cooked down to make tomato sauce.

entries.clue: Brahms and Liszt agree with poor chap off to Bayreuth (9)

indicatorNotes.Brahms and Liszt: rhyming slang for 'pissed', drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

annotation.surface: Two composers find themselves agreeing with a poor man heading to the Wagner festival.
annotation.walkthrough: Brahms and Liszt is Cockney rhyming slang for 'pissed' (drunk), not the composers. Bayreuth in Germany hosts the annual Wagner opera festival.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone travelling to Bayreuth is going to the opera festival, so is an operagoer.

entries.clue: Inside of dock, defendant’s first caught by forensic traces and shuts off (8)

annotation.type: container + charade + middle letters + first letter

indicatorNotes.caught by: something caught by another is held in its grip, so D sits inside CLUES

blocks.note: clues = traces left for forensic investigators

annotation.surface: In court, forensic evidence against the man in the dock seals off his defence.
annotation.walkthrough: The courtroom surface makes 'dock' look like the place a defendant stands; only its middle letters are used.
annotation.definitionFit: To occlude is to block or shut off, as a cloud occludes the sun.

entries.clue: Maybe fly where Mormon can be found? (6)

blocks.note: 'maybe' marks a definition by example: a fly is one of a class
split in two: a Mormon is found inside a religious group

annotation.surface: Someone wonders whether a fly is where a Mormon might be spotted.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the split reading IN SECT. Mormon is also the name of a butterfly, which ties the halves together.
annotation.definitionFit: A fly is an example of an insect, which 'Maybe' signals.

entries.clue: A dame packing heat put blade away (7)

blocks.note: a dame is a woman: SHE

annotation.surface: An armed woman carrying a gun decides to put her knife away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Packing heat' is slang for carrying a gun, which makes the phrase look like a single idea; 'packing' is the container instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A sheath is the case a knife or sword is kept in, so returning the blade to it puts the blade away.

entries.clue: University lecturer initially enraged after 50% cut in school education programme (8)

indicatorNotes.initially: take the first letters of 'University lecturer enraged'
indicatorNotes.after: the initials come after the other pieces
indicatorNotes.50% cut in: school is cut in half, leaving SCH

blocks.note: first letters of University, Lecturer, Enraged

annotation.surface: A university lecturer is furious about halved school funding.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Initially' seems to modify 'enraged' alone, but it takes the first letter of all three words before it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a timetable of events is both a schedule and a programme.

entries.clue: Employ uniform floor covering element around island (7)

indicatorNotes.around: to put one thing around another is to surround it, so TILE wraps IS

blocks.note: U = uniform in the NATO alphabet
one tile is an element of a tiled floor

annotation.surface: A builder is told to use standard floor tiles around an island unit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Island' reads as a kitchen island in the flooring surface; it is only the abbreviation IS.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to put something to use.

entries.clue: One of two - one of two 8s (6)

blocks.note: the word for one or the other of a pair
8 down is PRONUNCIATION: this word has two, EE-ther and EYE-ther

annotation.surface: A puzzle about choosing one of two options, and one of two numbered items.
annotation.walkthrough: The word 'either' is itself sung both ways in 'Let's Call the Whole Thing Off', the song behind 8, 9 and 15.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are the one word: the pronoun for either of a pair, and a word famous for its two pronunciations.

entries.clue: Rotating cylinder made to bend inside pipe (9)

indicatorNotes.to bend: MADE is bent into a new shape
indicatorNotes.inside: the rearranged letters go inside TRILL

blocks.note: to pipe or trill is to sing in a high warble, like a bird

annotation.surface: A spinning cylinder is forced to bend inside a pipe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pipe' looks like the tube a cylinder would sit in, but it is the verb meaning to sing shrilly.
annotation.definitionFit: The original treadmill was a large rotating cylinder turned by people or animals walking on it.

entries.clue: Being there, but not at 10 to 2 (5)

annotation.definitionNote: 2 down is ART FORM; dance is one

indicatorNotes.but not: remove the letters that follow from the word

blocks.note: AT + TEN, removed from the front

annotation.surface: Someone is present, but not at ten minutes to two.
annotation.walkthrough: '10 to 2' looks like a time of day; it is really '10' for the wordplay and '2' pointing at 2 down, ART FORM.
annotation.definitionFit: Dance is an art form, the answer to 2 down.

entries.clue: A young woman’s unsuitable (5)

blocks.note: the title for an unmarried young woman

annotation.surface: A young woman is judged unsuitable.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is' and joins the wordplay to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Amiss means wrong or out of place, so unsuitable.

entries.clue: With frequency not satisfactory in intro, more piano (5)

indicatorNotes.not: 'not' says the letter for satisfactory is absent, so it is removed
indicatorNotes.in intro: the letter removed is the first one

blocks.note: piano = soft in music, so to make more piano is to soften
S = satisfactory, a school grade; removed from the start

annotation.surface: A music teacher, unhappy with the opening, asks for it quieter, again and again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Piano' is the musical instruction for soft, not the instrument.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something that happens frequently happens often.

entries.clue: Hole up around yard with rocks when eavesdropping - this is basic (9)

indicatorNotes.around: HIDE goes around the other letters
indicatorNotes.when eavesdropping: an eavesdropper hears the word, so it is spelt by its sound

blocks.note: to hole up is to hide

annotation.surface: A spy hides out in a rocky yard, listening in, and calls it the basics.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Basic' is the chemistry sense: a hydroxide is a base, the opposite of an acid.
annotation.definitionFit: Hydroxides such as sodium hydroxide are bases, so a hydroxide is literally basic.

entries.clue: Try once more, sing away in practising for performance (6)

indicatorNotes.away: SING goes away from the longer word

annotation.surface: A singer is told to try again, dropping the singing during rehearsals.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Try' is the legal sense: a court that rehears a case tries it again.
annotation.definitionFit: Legal sense: courts 'try' cases, and hearing a case again means trying it once more.

entries.clue: Iced dessert in solidified state, round sphere (6)

indicatorNotes.round: to go round something is to encircle it, so SET encircles ORB

blocks.note: set = solidified, as a jelly sets

annotation.surface: A frozen dessert, set solid, is served as a round ball.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Round sphere' reads as a scoop of dessert; 'round' is the container instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A sorbet is an iced dessert made from fruit juice or purée.
